name: Oats
summary: Oats are rarely grown in the Philippines, where oatmeal is imported. A few highland farms sow small plots, mostly as green feed for animals or as a cover crop, and this short guide shows how they do it.
season: Sown in the highlands at the end of the rains, around October to December, so the crop grows in the cool, dry months.
material: Dry seed bought from feed or seed suppliers, sown without soaking.
spacing: Rows about 20 to 25 cm apart, sown thinly, or broadcast.
water: Grown on the last of the rains, with hand watering in dry spells.
fertilizer: Compost or manure at sowing, with some complete fertilizer (14 14 14) on poor soil.
care: Hand weeding in the first month. Plots grown for feed are cut and fed fresh.
harvest: Grain is ready at about 90 to 110 days when the heads are pale and dry. Feed oats are cut green, before the heads ripen.

ways.label: Sown direct in rows or broadcast

steps.title: Dig or plow to a fine bed
steps.how: Plow or dig the plot, clear the weeds and rake it fine.

steps.title: Sow the seed
steps.how: Sow thinly in shallow rows about 20 to 25 cm apart and cover with 3 to 5 cm of soil, or scatter and rake in.

steps.title: Manure at sowing
steps.how: Work compost or manure into the bed, with some complete fertilizer (14 14 14) on poor soil.

steps.title: Water if dry
steps.how: Water the plot if no rain falls in the first days.

steps.title: Weed
steps.how: Hand pull the weeds while the plants are young.

steps.title: Cut when the heads are dry
steps.how: For grain, cut when the heads have turned pale and the grain is firm. For feed, cut the green plants before the heads ripen.

steps.title: Dry and thresh
steps.how: Sun dry the bundles, beat out the grain and winnow it.

ways.note: The days count to a grain harvest. Oats cut green for animal feed are taken much earlier, before the heads ripen.

mistakes: Sowing in the lowlands or in the rainy season.
Sowing too thickly, which gives weak stems.
Leaving ripe heads out in the rain.
better: Use seed of a variety meant for warm highlands.
Sow only in the cool dry months.
Test the soil and add compost to poor ground.
Keep the plot weed free for the first month.

watering.traditional: Oats are rare here and grown on small highland plots sown at the end of the rains. Growers water by hand in dry spells.
watering.method: Hand watering with a can or a hose on small plots, in the morning.
watering.rainfed: Sow at the end of the rains, from October to December, while the soil is still moist.
watering.dryseason: Water small plots about once a week in dry spells. For green feed, keep watering until cutting.
watering.wet: Plant on beds that drain, since wet, warm weather brings rust and lodging.

schedule.often: Water right after sowing and every few days if no rain falls
schedule.amount: Enough to moisten the seed rows, never soggy
schedule.why: Even moisture brings an even stand.

schedule.often: In dry spells, water about once a week
schedule.amount: Soak the rows with a can or a hose
schedule.why: This is the green growth that feed oats are cut from.

schedule.amount: A good soaking of the rows

schedule.why: The heads must dry for cutting.

critical: Heading and grain filling, about day 45 to 85: a dry spell gives light grain.

signs.dry: Leaves roll and pale and the plants stay short.
signs.wet: Yellow leaves, rust spots and plants that fall over.

better: Water at tillering and at heading if you can water only twice.
